diagram_math_checks.objects_and_maps: For delta nonzero, E_2: TL_3(C,delta) -> TL_2(C,delta) is delta^-1 times right closure, as defined in def-temperley-lieb-diagram-tower-and-right-closure. Every top input has three labeled-by-position endpoints on each side; every lower output has two.
checks: Position indices increase left to right on both boundaries, as required by def-temperley-lieb-diagram-category. Each input has exactly three disjoint solid matching arcs and six endpoints; dashed arcs are added closure paths, not basis strands.
Column 1 pairs each t_i with b_i. Column 2 pairs t1-t2, b1-b2, t3-b3. Column 3 pairs t2-t3, b2-b3, t1-b1. These reproduce local F1 and the generator definition.

Column 4 pairs t1-t2, b2-b3, t3-b1; column 5 pairs t2-t3, b1-b2, t1-b3. The diagonal curves pass between the cap and cup without crossing either, agreeing with F1 and the left-factor-above convention for d1d2 and d2d1.

In each column the dashed exterior path connects t3 to b3. For columns 1 and 2 it closes the existing t3-b3 strand into precisely one cycle. The retained matchings are respectively 1_2 and d1, and delta^-1 delta=1 gives the first two displayed outputs, as in proof 1.1.
For column 3, t2-t3 followed by the dashed arc and b3-b2 becomes t2-b2, leaving t1-b1. There is no cycle, so the output is delta^-1 1_2.

For column 4, b2-b3 follows the closure path to t3 and then b1, yielding b2-b1; t1-t2 remains. For column 5, t2-t3 follows closure to b3 and then t1, yielding t2-t1; b1-b2 remains. Neither creates a cycle; both outputs are delta^-1 d1, consistent with proof 2.1.

The five arrows indicate evaluation by E_2, not composition of category morphisms with unequal boundary counts. No additional commutative square, oriented strand, crossing, or trace equality is asserted by the picture.
